# AmbiSQL: Interactive Ambiguity Detection and Resolution for Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#ambisql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.15276v2) · arXiv:2508.15276v2, 23 March 2026; author manuscript labeled SIGMOD-Companion 2026

**Reading coverage:** All four PDF pages, Sections 1-4, taxonomy, technical details, demonstration text and Figures 1-3 captions/UI descriptions. No appendices present.

## Research question

Ambiguous phrases can map to different schema elements or depend on unstated external reasoning choices. The system aims to expose those choices before SQL generation.

## Method

A seven-type taxonomy separates database/schema/value/operation ambiguity from source, context, premise and reference ambiguity. Prompted detection produces multiple-choice clarification, including free-text Other and skip/Abstain options. A taxonomy-organized preference tree stores replies; later constraints override earlier ones and rewritten queries are checked again.

## Evaluation

This is a system demonstration integrated with XiYan-SQL, with 40 curated BIRD/TAG examples and customizable queries/databases. The paper illustrates side-by-side query comparison, rather than a controlled aggregate accuracy or user-study evaluation.

## What the results support

The walkthrough shows how user choices modify schema mappings, time constraints and additional filters. It demonstrates an interaction design and state-management mechanism, not general accuracy gains.

## Limits and qualifications

Coverage depends on prompted detection and the supplied taxonomy. Claims that refinement resolves all dependent ambiguities are architectural aims; no formal guarantee, broad benchmark comparison or real-user outcome study establishes them.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful for clarification interfaces and dependent ambiguity handling; its skip option is a user action, distinct from model refusal on an unanswerable request.
